Choose between the longer challenges (45 km or 60 km), with routes taking you through Kolmården Forest, up onto Kvarseboklint’s mountain ridge and down to the shore of Bråviken, onward past the natural surroundings of Nävsjön, and finally through the technical Bråviksbranten before the finish. The race combines technical trails, boardwalks across bogs and spectacular views, with well-equipped aid stations along the way. The organizer emphasizes safety and mandatory equipment, as well as a medal and light refreshments at the finish.
course_highlights: Kvarseboklint’s impressive mountain ridge with views
Descent to the shore of Bråviken and passage by Nävsjön, with boardwalks across vast bogs
Technical and demanding running through the Bråviksbranten Nature Reserve
additional: Mandatory equipment: mobile phone, running vest/backpack with fluids (at least 0.5 L), pressure bandage/blood-stopping dressing, and a map with the emergency number (provided at bib collection). Aid stations: 45K = 4; 60K = 5 (detailed stations with different energy products are listed for the 48 km variant). Bib collection from 05:30; bibs must be collected at least 30 minutes before the start. The course is marked with large orange arrows and flagging tape. Light refreshments and a custom-designed medal are included at the finish; massage is available at cost. Energy and fluids provided in partnership with Umara. Mandatory equipment; start times: 45K 08:00; cutoff time 13:30 at 44 km; aid stations: 45K = 4, 60K = 5; finish: a meal is included in the entry fee.

name: Läckövarvet
organizer: Kroppslabbet; Språng träning & äventyr; Stiftelsen Läckö Slott
description: Welcome to Läckövarvet, a running race starting and finishing at the magnificent Läckö Castle on Kållandsö. The race is offered over 21 km and 10 km, as well as a 2 km children’s race, and features varied terrain with forest trails, gravel roads and short sections of asphalt, along with views of Lake Vänern. The course passes well-known places such as Spiken Fishing Harbour and Roparudden, and finishes with a lap through the moat around the castle. The race is aimed at both competitive runners and families looking to enjoy a nature-rich, cultural and historic running experience.
course_highlights: Varied terrain: forest trails, gravel roads and short sections of asphalt
The course passes Spiken Fishing Harbour and the technical, scenic trails at Roparudden (cliffs and winding paths)
Start and finish at Läckö Castle, with a final lap through the moat and the finish line in front of the castle gate
additional: Courses start outside Läckö Castle; refreshments/energy supplies along the course; medical care and showers on site; lunch package for 165 kr after the finish; parking 50 kr; taking the bus to the race is recommended; included in the Västsvenska Löparcupen.

name: Mörksuggejakten TrailRun
description: Mörksuggejakten is a classic race in the long-distance cycling cup in Rättvik, enjoyed by elite cyclists and recreational riders alike. The main course is available as a 72 km route or a shortened 44 km version, featuring varied terrain with gravel roads, trails and some challenging climbs, as well as fine views over Siljan. The route passes places such as Vidablick, the Hedsåsen summer farm, the Enån valley with its narrow suspension bridges, and Dalhalla and Springkällan. The event also includes Lilla Mörksuggejakten for young riders at the Jarl area and is organised by IK Jarl.
course_highlights: Main course: 72 km (or a shorter 44 km option)
Views over Siljan from Vidablick and the Hedsåsen summer farm
Sections along the Enån valley with narrow suspension bridges; passes Dalhalla and Springkällan
additional: Registration for race categories is via RaceWeb; late registration is handled on RaceWeb between 08:30 and 12:00 (Lilla Mörksuggan). Bib collection for Lilla Mörksuggan: Jarlstugan, Saturday 5 July, 09:00–11:30. Bibs with chips are used in race categories and recreational/family categories (children's, recreational/family categories are not timed). A technical zone/feeding station is located in the arena between the start and finish zones; medical staff will be on site (contact person: Josefin Linell, tel. 076-796 39 69). Changing rooms and showers are available at Jarlstugan. Mörksuggejakten TrailRun was first held in 2017. The race is part of the Mörksuggejakten events in Rättvik and is coordinated with Lilla Mörksuggejakten; late registration and bib collection are planned in connection with 4 July 2026.

name: Semesterhalvmaran
location: Fjugesta, Laxå Municipality, Örebro County, Sweden
description: The Vacation Half Marathon is a summer race organized by running club LK Gränslöst, giving runners the opportunity to experience the beautiful open landscapes of the Närke Plain. The course often follows gravel roads among rolling grain fields, offering a nature-close, summery running experience. LK Gränslöst is an inclusive club that welcomes runners of all levels.
course_highlights: Gravel roads across the Närke Plain
Rolling grain fields and open views
A summer vacation-time race with a relaxed, nature-close feel
additional: LK Gränslöst organizes several summer races: the Vacation Half Marathon, the Summer Ten-Kilometer, and the children’s race Solruset. The club announced that the races would be paused in 2025 because key people in the organizing group were unavailable. The club also holds open Wednesday training sessions at 18:00 in Örebro (location varies), led by Carina Gustavsson and Thomas Stenius.

name: Gotland Run 511k (2026)
description: Gotland Run 511k is more of a running adventure than a traditional race: a self-supported journey around Gotland of approximately 511 km, starting and finishing in Visby. Participants follow a clockwise loop that also includes a circuit of Fårö, with support from four so-called Angel Stations along the way. The organizer provides some basic services, but runners are responsible for most food and logistics arrangements. The entire route must be completed on foot within 10 days, with regular position reports throughout the day.
course_highlights: Circular route around Gotland (starting and finishing in Visby), including a circuit of Fårö
Most of the route follows Gotlandsleden: long stretches of asphalt, gravel roads, and shorter sections of trail
Four Angel Stations along the course offering water, support, and sometimes the opportunity for a short rest or a bed
additional: Self-supported format: the organizer provides only the most basic services; participants are responsible for food and most accommodation. A pre-race dinner and race briefing in Visby on the evening before the start are mandatory. One night’s accommodation at Visby Fängelse Hostel and breakfast on race morning are included, as are a race bib, luggage storage during the race, and a souvenir for finishers. Transport back to Visby is available for participants who withdraw. Participants must report their position twice daily (10:00 and 22:00) using an online check-in tool and a Google Maps link. The overall time limit is 10 days (an average of ~51 km per day). The information page has sections on mandatory equipment and basic rules. History: the first edition in 2023 had 5 starters and 3 finishers. Distance approximately 511 km (318 miles); four Angel Stations along the way; no pacing; mandatory equipment; pre-race dinner and briefing; one night’s accommodation in Visby included; luggage storage; race bib; transport back to Visby if withdrawing; finishers receive a souvenir.

name: Västervik City Run
description: Västervik City Run is a 6.2 km city race in and around central Västervik, starting and finishing at Grönsaks- och Fiskartorget. The course consists of two loops of approximately 3 km, with the lap point at Fiskaretorget. The race has been held since 2011 and traditionally takes place on the Monday of week 28, starting at 20:00. It is well established in Västervik and attracts runners of different ages.
course_highlights: 6.2 km city race (two loops of approximately 3 km)
Start and finish at Grönsaks- och Fiskartorget
Lap point at Fiskaretorget
additional: The children’s race (Sparbanksloppet) is an 800 m fun run for children up to age 10, with a group start from Fiskaretorget at 18:30. The children’s race starts level with the Stegeholm Castle ruins, by the sun deck and Myntbryggan, and follows the cycle path along Gamlebyviken to the finish at Grönsakstorget. Participants receive a medal after finishing. Bib collection is at ICA Maxi or the race office; advance registration closes on 3 July at 16:00; registration on race day is open from 13:00 to 19:00.

name: Nordansjö Nattultra
location: Norbergs OK:s klubbstuga, Nordansjö 24, Norberg, Sweden
description: Nordansjö Nattultra is a nature-focused ultrarunning experience taking place on the night of 10–11 July 2026, with the main 60 km race consisting of five loops. The race is organised by Norbergs OK, starting and finishing at the club’s cabin in Nordansjö. It is suitable for both experienced ultrarunners and runners looking to try a longer summer challenge. The course is easy to run and designed to offer an enjoyable summer experience combining camaraderie and competition. A warm welcome to the second edition of Nordansjö Nattultra!
course_highlights: Five loops of 12 km each (60 km total)
Mainly right-of-way roads/gravel roads, plus approximately 2.7 km on an illuminated trail
The course is run clockwise and includes a descent down Håberget five times
additional: Mandatory equipment: headlamp and mobile phone. The time limit for 60 km is 10 hours; runners finish after five loops (5×12 km). Race bibs can be collected from 19:00 on Friday 10 July at the club cabin. Aid stations are located at the start/finish and halfway around the course (6 km); no disposable cups are provided—bring your own soft flask or cup. Finishers receive a finisher cap, medal and breakfast at the club cabin. Maximum 100 starters (first come, first served). Håberget mountain prize; start/finish at Norbergs OK’s club cabin in Nordansjö (Nordansjö 24, Norberg); maximum 100 participants; aid stations at the start, finish and halfway; no cups are provided—bring your own cup; registration opened 2025-09-01.

name: Musköloppet
location: Muskö Hembygdsgård, Muskö, Haninge kommun, Stockholms län, Sverige
description: Musköloppet is a long-standing running race in a spectacular archipelago setting, starting and finishing at Muskö Local Heritage Centre/Muskö IF’s clubhouse. The race usually attracts around 300 runners (about 400 including the youngest children) and has a friendly, homecoming atmosphere, with many taking the opportunity to meet relatives and neighbours. The event offers children’s and youth classes as well as recreational classes (5 km and 10 km) on varied surfaces, and takes place on Saturday, 11 July 2026.
course_highlights: Start/finish at Muskö Local Heritage Centre, near the clubhouse, outdoor gym and hockey rink
Course surfaces: approximately 50% asphalt, 30–40% gravel and 10% trail
The 5 km and 10 km courses are officially measured (course measurer Mikael Hill, 240523); this year, the 10 km is run as a single loop
additional: Late registration is available at the start/finish area up to one hour before the race starts. Food and drinks are available at the start/finish. Directions by car and public transport, as well as parking information, are available on the “Find us” page. Around 300 runners usually take part (about 400 including the youngest children). Start/finish area at Muskö Local Heritage Centre/Muskö IF’s clubhouse; 5 km and 10 km courses with varied surfaces (approximately 50% asphalt, 40% gravel and 10% trail on one course; approximately 60% asphalt, 30% gravel and 10% trail on the other); merchandise, kiosk snacks, coffee, soft drinks and food from Micke’s Grill; late registration at the finish area up to one hour before the race starts.

name: Lidingöloppet Funäsfjällen
description: Lidingöloppet in Funäsfjällen is “Sweden’s most beautiful challenge” — a trail race featuring steep climbs, sloping trails, open meadows and sweeping mountain views. The third edition takes place on 11 July 2026, offering an unbeatable combination of adrenaline and nature experiences. Welcome to Bruksvallarna Ski Stadium. Register via the Lidingöloppet website and collect your race bib at the venue.
course_highlights: Steep climbs and challenging mountain terrain
Sloping trails and flat meadows
Sweeping mountain views and panoramic vistas
additional: Registration is via the Lidingöloppet website; race bibs are collected at the venue in Bruksvallarna. A 100 kr fee applies to registrations made on race day (Saturday). The week before the race, Bruksvallarnas Running Week features shoe testing, running clinics, children’s activities, after-run events and an expo at Arena Syd outside Bruksvallarnas Sportcenter. Results become official and final one week after the race. By registering, you agree to have your name published in start and results lists and to images being used in the event’s channels; requests for exceptions are handled by the event office (info@lidingoloppet.se). Seeding and start times; accommodation in Ramundberget near the start; logistical facilities such as parking, water stations, and food and drink; a week in July with programme and accommodation information at bruksvallsliden.se/lidingoloppet; children’s race/adventure for younger participants

name: Klåveröd Backyard 2026
description: Klåveröd Backyard 2026 is an event published on Facebook in Svalöv, taking place on Saturday, 11 July 2026, and created by Linda Bengtsson. The event is associated with Klåveröds Ski Club and is presented on an official Facebook event page. It is located in Klåveröd near Söderåsen, offering trail and forest running in a natural setting. For details and contact information, see the event page on Facebook.
course_highlights: Running in Klåveröd/Svalöv near Söderåsen
Trail and forest terrain (event organized through Klåveröds Ski Club)
Close to the natural areas and national park area of Söderåsen
additional: Organizer/creator: Linda Bengtsson; event associated with Klåveröds Ski Club; the main information page and invitation are on the Facebook event page: https://www.facebook.com/events/1496584765165217/; Klåveröd's Facebook group and page are used for local information. At the previous Klåveröd Backyard in 2024, Jonas Elmer won with 14 laps, approximately 90 km in total.

name: Victorialoppet
price_range: 175-550 kr beroende på kategori och registreringsdatum
description: Victorialoppet is an annual running festival in Borgholm, celebrating its 45th year in 2026. The event offers several distances for all ages and abilities, including the 9 km main race, the 4 km Victoriajoggen, the 2 km Lilla Victorialoppet, and Mini for the youngest participants. The course is fast and easy to run, with beautiful coastal views and an enthusiastic crowd. The event is a festive celebration, with music along the course and a welcoming atmosphere for participants and spectators alike.
course_highlights: Fast, easy-to-run 9 km course with coastal views
Music at several points along the course
Courses for all ages, including para-sport categories
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 10:00 to 18:00 on race day at Borgholm Sports Hall. Changing rooms and showers are available for men and boys at the sports hall, and for women and girls at Viktoriaskolan’s gymnasium. Water is provided along the 9 km course, and participants receive refreshments after the finish. Timing uses disposable chips for most races; timing is optional for Victoriajoggen and the para-sport categories. Children in Lilla Victorialoppet receive a medal, ice cream, and a drink after the finish. The event runs from early afternoon into the evening, with several start times and races. Distances include 9 km, 4 km, 2 km, and 1.5 km, with participants from different age groups and disability categories. The event takes place in Borgholm’s sports area and includes both competitive and recreational races, as well as fundraising for charitable causes.

name: Kraftprovet
organizer: Trollhättans IF Friidrott och Trollhättans SOK
description: Kraftprovet is a classic city race in the heart of Trollhättan, celebrating its 40th anniversary on 17 July 2026. The course follows the canal through leafy surroundings and varied, hilly terrain, with beautiful views of the Göta älv, the locks and the historic power stations. The race brings together elite runners and recreational runners and creates a festive atmosphere with spectators, music and activities for the whole family. It is organised by Trollhättans IF Friidrott and Trollhättans SOK.
course_highlights: The course follows the canal area and the locks and waterfalls area in Trollhättan
Varied, hilly terrain with marked kilometre points
Views of the Göta älv, the locks and historic power stations
additional: Start and finish at Hansenplatsen in Trollhättan. Race bibs and T-shirts can be collected at the start/finish area from 10:00; collection closes 30 minutes before each start. Names will be printed on race bibs for entries submitted by 30 June. Functional T-shirts can be ordered when registering by 15 May (included for Kraftprovet 11.6 km and Specialprovet; costs 130 kr for the other races). Specialprovet welcomes assistants/guides at no extra cost. Kraftprovet has pacers for 50, 55 and 60 minutes; Fun Run is untimed. Silver medals are awarded for times under 50:00 (men) and 55:00 (women). The costume contest gathers at 15:45, with a prize pool for the best costume. The 40th anniversary features new race elements; Knatteprovet, Miniprovet and the 800 m race are also on offer. This year's T-shirt can be purchased when registering.

name: Helags Fjällmara
distance_verbose: Marathon, 23 km, 12 km, 5 km, 3000 meter, 0.8 km
description: Helags Fjällmara is a classic mountain trail race in the Ljungdalsfjällen, held since 1985. The event offers several distances for different levels, from a children’s race to longer mountain trail races, with beautiful views and challenging trails. The start and finish are in the meadow in the centre of Ljungdalen, creating a welcoming race venue for both elite runners and families. The event is organised by volunteers from Ljungdalens Gymnastik och Idrottsförening.
course_highlights: Mountain terrain with beautiful views and challenging trails
Start and finish in the meadow in Ljungdalen
Several distances for different levels (23 km, 12 km, 5 km, 3 km and 800 m)
additional: Practical information: registration is open until 16/7 (no on-site late registration); registration for the children’s race is open until 18/7 at 10:15. Participant limits: 23 km 250 participants, 12 km 200, 5 km 150, 3 km 100, 800 m 200. The entry fee includes energy and water stations along the course, a personal cup from Umara (bring it during the race), electronic timing (chip in the race bib) and a medal for everyone who finishes. Showers and a sauna are available after the finish. Registration is binding; transferring an entry and changing category are possible for a change fee of 250 kr (changes are made as instructed by email; the registration page lists both info@ljungdalensgif.se and hej@helagsfjallmara.se as contacts). Competition categories for elite runners, recreational runners and children; registration takes place via raceweb on the website; several distances are available: 42 km, 23 km, 12 km, 5 km, 3 km and 800 m.

name: Hornsjön Runt
location: Pensionat Hornsjön, Löttorp, Borgholm Municipality, Kalmar County, Sweden
description: Hornsjön Runt is a family-friendly running event around Öland’s only inland lake, through beautiful and varied scenery. Organised by Högby IF, it offers distances for children and young people, 5.5 km, 11 km, and a non-timed walking class. The start and finish are at Pensionat Hornsjön, and everyone who completes the event receives a medal. The event combines a long tradition with scenic routes over gravel, sand dunes, forest, and open pastures.
course_highlights: Around Öland’s only inland lake (Hornsjön)
Varied terrain: gravel with Öland limestone, grass, and sand dunes
Passes cow pastures and deciduous and coniferous forest; three water stations along the course
additional: Register by 11 July 2026. Late registration is available through 16 July, followed by the option to register when race bibs are distributed from 12:00 on race day. The non-timed walking class starts between 13:00 and 16:00. There are three water stations along the course, plus refreshments at the start/finish. Showers and changing facilities are available at Högby sports ground. Prizes are awarded to the top three in all classes, with additional prizes drawn at random. Start times: youth classes 15:30; 5.5 km 17:00; 11 km 17:05. The walking class is available over 5.5 or 11 km, with starts between 13:00 and 16:00. Showers and changing facilities are available at Högby sports ground.

name: Bohusläns Saltaste
location: Hamburgö, Tanum Municipality, Västra Götaland County, Sweden

name: Runmaröloppen 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Mini-Lunken 1.5km 60kr inkl nummerlapp, medalj och en kula glass.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Lunken 5.7km: från 150kr inkl nummerlapp, medalj och finisherdryck.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Halvmarathon 21km: från 350kr inkl nummerlapp, medalj och finisherdryck.

description: RUNmaröloppen is a family-friendly race in the heart of the Stockholm archipelago on Runmarö, starting and finishing at the Svängen inn. The event offers short children’s races, Lunken (5.7 km) and a half marathon (21 km) along beautiful trails, open fields and through archipelago villages—perfect for a day trip by Waxholmsbolaget boats. The races have limited participant numbers and place great emphasis on atmosphere, aid stations and sustainability; 20% of the surplus goes to the Archipelago Foundation.
course_highlights: Half marathon (21 km) around the whole of Runmarö, with views towards Sandhamn
A mix of trail paths, gravel roads and archipelago villages; two trail sections on the half marathon
Permanent course signs and 1 km markers on the half marathon, as well as many local aid stations
additional: Start and finish at the Svängen inn (about 400 m from the pier). Mini-Lunken starts at 11:00; Lunken and the Half Marathon start at 13:00. The half marathon has 1 km markers, an interactive map, a total elevation gain of 169 m and several local refreshment stations (for example, Nore with pickled cucumber and Solberga). Mini-Lunken participants get an ice cream; everyone receives a medal and a post-race drink. Race entries are limited (200 places for the half marathon and 120 for Lunken in the first release, with a further 30 places released closer to race day, often at 18:00 the day before). Registration opens on 1 May at 09:00. 20% of the surplus is donated to the Archipelago Foundation. Results are published online and the awards ceremony takes place after the races; in the evening, there is dinner and a party at Svängen. Start and finish at Svängen; courses marked; registration opens 1 May at 09:00; places are limited (200 for the Half Marathon, 120 for Lunken in the first release, plus 30 additional places later); a strong charitable focus and local atmosphere.

name: Löttorpsvarvet
location: First Camp Löttorp, Löttorp, Öland, Sweden
description: Löttorpsvarvet is a family-friendly cross-country race held at First Camp Löttorp on Öland. The main distance is 6.2 km, and the course runs through woodland and meadows, with beautiful views of the Baltic Sea. Youth races of 1.4 km and 800 m are available for younger runners, and all finishers receive a medal. The event is organised by Högby IF and welcomes both recreational runners and young athletes.
course_highlights: 6.2 km of scenic cross-country running around First Camp Löttorp
Run through woodland and meadows with views of the Baltic Sea
Youth courses: 1.4 km and 800 m
additional: Register by 15 July 2026. Late registration is open until 20 July; after that, you can register when collecting your race bib on race day (from 15:00). Late registration fee: SEK 300 for Men/Women and SEK 200 for Children/Youth. Payment accepted by cash, card or Swish. Children’s/youth classes: P/F7 (800 m), P/F9, P/F11 and P/F13 (1.4 km), with separate start times; classes for ages 11 and under have no timing or prize-giving. All finishers receive a medal. Information: Jonne Svensson 070-693 87 44, Calle Nilsson 070-444 31 02. Register by 15 July 2026; late registration until 20 July; after that, at race-bib collection on race day from 15:00. Late registration fee: SEK 300 (Men/Women), SEK 200 (Children/Youth). Classes P/F11 and younger have no timing or prize-giving. Cross-country race at First Camp Löttorp, with start times for different age groups: P/F7 (800 m), P/F9 (1.4 km), P/F11 (1.4 km) and P/F13 (1.4 km).

name: Falkenbergs Stadslopp

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 400 kr fram till och med 14:e juli 2026.

description: Falkenbergs Stadslopp is a popular 10 km road race through Falkenberg’s central streets and green spaces. The race takes place on Saturday, 25 July 2026, with a mass start at 12:00, and is suitable for both experienced runners and recreational participants. In 2026, the course has been rerouted because of municipal work at Doktorspromenaden. The event has a festive atmosphere, with spectators cheering along the course. It has been held for more than 40 years and is part of Tour de Falkenberg.
course_highlights: 10 km through the city centre and green spaces
New course route in 2026 because of work at Doktorspromenaden
Start at Falkenbergs Idrottsplats (new start location) and finish in the city centre at Nygatan / Stortorget
additional: One distance: 10 km, with separate women’s and men’s categories; the course is officially measured by the Swedish Athletics Association. The prize ceremony is at approximately 13:00, and every finisher receives a medal. Self-seeded mass start, with start corrals marked by pace flags (e.g. 4:30/km). Water is available at the start and at two aid stations along the course. Race bibs can be collected at Team Sportia (Lokstallarna, Sandgatan 40) on Thursday and Friday of race week from 12:00 to 18:00, and at the start area on Saturday from 9:00. Bag drop is available at the start area from 10:00; bags must be collected by 15:00. Entry fees are non-refundable, but the organisers can help with name changes. The race is part of Tour de Falkenberg and is the 2026 district championship. The 10 km course runs through central Falkenberg; the start is on Läroverksgatan and the finish is at Nygatan/Stortorget. The course has been changed for 2026 because of Doktorspromenaden.

name: Bjäre Trail
description: Bjäre Trail is a trail race on the beautiful Bjäre Peninsula, featuring a very hilly course along the northern side of Hallandsåsen. You run through Sinarpsdalen, dense beech forests with rushing waterfalls, and past grazing pastures, a disused ski slope and an old railway—the course offers many magical views. The website lists several distances (12 km, 17 km, 34 km and 51 km) and a children’s race. You are welcome to register and enjoy a challenging trail experience close to nature.
course_highlights: A very hilly course along the northern side of Hallandsåsen
Passes through Sinarpsdalen and dense beech forests with rushing waterfalls
Features grazing pastures, a disused ski slope and an old railway, with magical views
additional: Start and finish at Båstad Företagsby, Ängelholmsvägen 269, 42 Båstad. The children’s/junior race is approximately 2,000 m. Register on site (cash or Swish) for 60 kr. The website offers race information, a start list, previous results and a GPS file (.gpx) of the course. Maximum 300 participants; register via the website; the regular registration deadline is one week before the start; late registration is available on race day for an additional fee. Race numbers can be collected at the start/finish no later than one hour before the start, or at Bjäre bär’s farm shop. Toilets are available in the business park; there are no changing rooms or showers. Travel by Skånetrafiken is recommended.

name: Hamra Trail Run 2026
description: Hamra Trail Run is a small, friendly trail race in stunning mountain surroundings, focused on the experience rather than a mass start. The race offers three distances—Sprint 12 km, Distance 24 km and Ultra 48 km—and starts at Pensionat Strandgården in Fjällnäs, Tänndalen. With a limited number of places (maximum 150), the organizers invite runners to enjoy views from Skenörsfjället, a sense of community and a runners’ dinner after the finish.
course_highlights: The courses mostly follow existing trails and paths through mountain terrain
Climb up and down Skenörsfjället, with views towards Malmagsvålen
Start and bib pickup at Pensionat Strandgården, Fjällnäs
additional: Mandatory equipment: your own cup (no disposable cups at the aid stations), an extra warm layer for your upper body, a wind jacket (and wind pants if needed), a buff, a first-aid kit including an elastic bandage, and a mobile phone with the safety number saved. Maximum 150 participants; registration is via MittLopp.se (links provided by the organizer). GPX files and a race guide with the safety number and practical information will be published ahead of the race. After the race, there will be a get-together and prize-giving at 15:00, followed by a runners’ dinner. Shoes with spikes or metal studs are not allowed; first-aid-trained marshals will be stationed along the course. Maximum 150 start places; registration via MittLopp.se; GPX files in the Runner’s Guide to HTR; pre-race briefing 30 minutes before the start outside Strandgården; aid stations along the course; accommodation at Strandgården or in Fjällnäs; After Run and runners’ dinner; start times: 48k 08:00, 24k 10:00, 12k 11:30.

name: Salomon 27K
location: Ottsjö, Åre Municipality, Jämtland County, Sweden
description: Salomon 27K is a 27 km mountain-running event that is part of Fjällmaratonveckan and crosses three mountains, finishing in the scenic village of Ottsjö. The race is described as picturesque and is considered by many to be one of Sweden’s most beautiful. The course is pure mountain terrain, with magnificent views and challenging running across mountain sections.
course_highlights: 27 kilometres of mountain terrain
Crosses three mountains
Finishes in scenic surroundings in Ottsjö
additional: Food and hydration stations along the course (see provisional menu); cup-free hydration stations with kåsa drinking vessels; bus transfers to the start from Ottsjö, Trillevallen and Undersåker, and back after the finish; electronic chip timing; mountain safety organisation; option to transfer a race entry for a fee (250 kr); recommendation to use the Startklar insurance. Results and live updates are available; race entries can be transferred if needed; sponsors include Kia and Fjälltransfer Partners

name: Peak Performance Vertical K
description: Peak Performance Vertical K is a prestigious, fast and demanding uphill race held every year on Tuesday evening during Kia Fjällmaraton. The race starts en masse from Åre Torg and finishes at the summit of Åreskutan, with exactly 1,000 vertical metres of elevation gain. Expect maximum effort from start to finish; the course records to beat are Emmie Collinge’s 46:24 and Kilian Jornet’s 39:13. The organiser works with Peak Performance, which has developed a training programme for those who want to prepare specifically for Vertical K.
course_highlights: Mass start from Åre Torg
Finish at the summit of Åreskutan — exactly 1,000 vertical metres of elevation gain
Fast, steep uphill course; course records: Emmie Collinge 46:24, Kilian Jornet 39:13
additional: Prize money is awarded to the top three in the men’s and women’s categories. The organiser has developed a six-week training programme in the Peak Performance Strava Club. A course image/map is published (map_verticalk.png on the website). According to sources, it is uniquely Sweden’s only vertical kilometre; it is part of Fjällmaratonveckan (Kia Fjällmaratonveckan) and AXA Fjällmaratonveckan, according to blog posts. The course is said to be approximately 5 km long according to the blog, and a training link is available via the Peak Performance Strava Club.

name: ATEA Kalmarmilen
description: ATEA Kalmarmilen is an established 10K race in Kalmar, held on 29 July 2026, and welcomes both recreational and elite runners. The race starts at Teatervallen and finishes at Larmtorget. The course passes Kalmar Castle, Stensö, the Old Town, the harbor, Fredrikskans, Lindö and Ängö before returning to the city centre for the final stretch. The race also has District Championship/Veteran District Championship status for Östsvenska and is organised by Högby IF. It is part of the I Run Kalmar race series. The children’s race, Lilla Atea Kalmarmilen, is held on the same day for different age groups, making it a family event with several running options.
course_highlights: Starts at Teatervallen and finishes at Larmtorget in Kalmar
The course passes landmarks including Kalmar Castle, the Old Town and the harbor
Illuminated running tracks and exercise trails in Kalmar; Lilla Atea Kalmarmilen for children is held at the same time
additional: Högby IF’s athletics page lists several upcoming races, including Kalmar Backyard Ultra, Skälbyloppet and Ölands Tjurrus, with dates and start times. The pages mention GPX files and a course map, as well as a walking category (Skälbyloppet: 4 km without timing) and separate start times for youth and senior categories. Race bib collection is at Kalmar Teater on 28 July from 15:00 to 17:00 and 29 July from 15:00 to 19:00. ICA MAXI provides drinks, fruit and chocolate after the race. Lilla Atea Kalmarmilen is held at the same time for children aged 2–13; the main race has a 10 km distance, as well as mini categories and distances for younger age groups.

name: Fjällmaraton 100k
description: Fjällmaraton 100K is a long, classic mountain run that starts at dawn in Fångåmon and is part of Kia Fjällmaraton Årefjällen. The first part of the course follows a beautiful, winding and runnable trail towards Vålådalen via Nulltjärn, before joining the classic Fjällmaraton route over the imposing Ottfjället. Runners continue over Hållfjället, Grofjället and Välliste on the way back to the finish in Ottsjö. The race is demanding and self-supported: participants must manage their own hydration and nutrition between the official aid stations.
course_highlights: Beautiful, winding and runnable trail towards Vålådalen via Nulltjärn
Classic climb over the imposing Ottfjället
Sections over Hållfjället, Grofjället and Välliste through mountain terrain
additional: All participants must be self-supported during the race: refill at official aid stations or use natural water sources; support outside the official stations is not permitted. Official sports drink: U Sport by Umara (lemon, mixed at 90 g/litre), with gluten-free U-bars available at the stations. Key stations and approximate distances: Vålådalen 22 km, Nordbottnen 38 km, Ottsjö (drop bag) 51.5 km, Tobaksdalen 65 km, Edsåsdalen 77.5 km, Skavhugget 82.5 km, Ytterstvallen 92.5 km, Finish 100 km. Post-race food is served by Fävikens Lanthandel. The organisers run Ottsjö 8K in the evening to create a great atmosphere at the finish. Drop bags are available in Ottsjö (51.5 km); U Sport by Umara sports drink and gluten-free U-bars are mentioned in the general information; start time 05:00; approximately 3,300 metres of elevation gain; transfer and travel options via Kia Fjälltransfer during Fjällmaraton Week.

name: Kia Fjällmaraton 45 km
description: Kia Fjällmaraton 45K is a demanding mountain marathon across classic mountain terrain, held during Fjällmaraton Week in the Åre area. The race dates back to 2005, and for 2026 the course is planned to cross Ottfjället along the event’s signature trail. The race welcomes both experienced mountain runners and curious beginners looking for an unusual and scenic challenge. To earn the well-known wooden medal, you must finish within the “medal time” (the winner’s time + 30%); all participants must be self-sufficient on the course.
course_highlights: The course crosses Ottfjället over classic mountain terrain
Food and hydration stations at Edsåsdalen (12 km, 25 km), Tobaksdalen (35.5 km), and Hållvallen (40 km)
Finish in Ottsjö, with a shared post-race lunch for all finishers
additional: Participants must be self-sufficient on the course; the official hydration product at the stations is Umara (2:1 lemon, 120 g/l). Water and toilets are available at the start in Trillevallen. Support along the course is not permitted except at the official stations. In addition to drinks, the stations offer bars, bananas, buns, and, at later stations, hot dogs, coffee, and broth. The race is approximately 45 km long with around 1,200 metres of elevation gain (according to a race report). Participants are self-sufficient between aid stations; official food and hydration are available at Edsåsdalen, Tobaksdalen, and Hållvallen. Kia offers Fjälltransfer, with free transfers between the finish and the parking area, as well as a bus between the finish and Undersåker/Åre. Accommodation in Åre near Kia Fjällmaraton includes, among other options, Hotel Åre Fjällsätra.

name: Stora Stöten Run
description: Stora Stöten Run is a trail race in the heart of the Falun Mine World Heritage Site, offering a historic and varied running experience. The course passes medieval smelting sites, mining farmsteads, dams and dam houses, following old routes known as Vattnets Väg till Gruvan (The Water’s Way to the Mine). The race has three distances (21.6 km, 13.6 km and 5.6 km) and welcomes both competitive runners and recreational participants, with the option to run timed or untimed. The event is organised by the orienteering club OK Kåre, which welcomes participants to the start and finish at Falun Mine.
course_highlights: Three courses: 21.6 km, 13.6 km and 5.6 km, starting and finishing at Falun Mine
The course passes medieval smelting sites, mining farmsteads, dams and dam houses along Vattnets Väg
Varied terrain: gravel, grass, trail tracks, nature paths and short paved sections; an initial climb and clearly marked downhill sections
additional: Start and finish at Falun Mine; warm-up begins at 12:10 on Falu Rödfärg’s paved area (approximately 7 minutes), led by Friskis & Svettis; all courses start at the same time, and runners are divided into two optional groups based on target pace (group 1: women ≤6 min/km, men ≤5 min/km). Runners can choose to run with or without timing; prizes go to the first three finishers on each course, with raffle prizes for other participants; teams can be registered (teams of 3), and registrations can be transferred free of charge through the registration system. The race information mentions aid stations/water stops, parking, race office, showers/changing facilities and course markings. All three courses start and finish at Falun Mine; results from previous years are available.

name: Ottsjö 12k
description: Ottsjö 12K is a 12 km mountain race with around 300 metres of elevation gain, offering a beautiful but demanding course through mountain terrain. It is an option for those who want to experience the mountain landscape without taking on the full distance or Salomon 27K. The route starts in Ottsjö and climbs towards Petterfjället and the Kläpphögarnas shelter, then continues along the plateau trail past Platåkåtan. It finishes by descending through the village and following Lake Ottsjön to the finish in the meadows in Ottsjö. The organiser offers a family option (children aged 10–13 run with an adult for SEK 200), and young people aged 14–18 pay half the entry fee.
course_highlights: Mountain terrain with around 300 metres of elevation gain
Climb towards Petterfjället and the Kläpphögarnas shelter, then follow the plateau trail past Platåkåtan
Descend through the village and follow Lake Ottsjön to the finish in the meadows in Ottsjö
additional: Start times are listed as 26/7 at 13:00 and 1/8 at 10:30. Children aged 10–13 can run with an adult for SEK 200; otherwise, the minimum age is 14. Young people aged 14–18 pay half the entry fee. Electronic chip timing; food and drink stations featuring local food; a traditional wooden cup is used at cup-free stations. Bus transfers to the start are available from Ottsjö, Trillevallen and Undersåker, with transfers back after the finish. 12 km, ~300 m elevation gain; start in Ottsjö; children’s option for ages 10–13 costs SEK 200 with an adult; minimum age 14; accompanying runners must stay in contact with minors; ages 14–18 pay half price; start times: 26/7 at 13:00 and 1/8 at 10:30.

name: Bruksleden Terrängmaraton
description: Welcome to Bruksleden Terrängmaraton, a friendly trail race along the beautiful Bruksleden on Saturday, 1 August 2026. The race offers two distances: 42 km (Helan) and 21 km (Halvan), and is suitable for both experienced trail runners and curious recreational runners. The courses pass through forests, along winding trails and by lakes, with varied and sometimes technically demanding terrain. The number of starting places is limited to preserve the welcoming atmosphere, and there are staffed checkpoints along the course. After finishing, showers and a light meal are available.
course_highlights: Running on Bruksleden’s winding forest trails
Sections passing lakes and beautiful forest scenery
Varied, sometimes technical terrain with steep climbs and descents
additional: Two distances: 42 km (Helan) and 21 km (Halvan). Limited number of starting places: 200. The deadline for standard registration is 17 July 2026; late registration is available through 30 July 2026 for a 50% surcharge. There are staffed checkpoints along the course for refills. Course profiles and routes (21 km and 42 km), as well as maps, are published on the organiser’s pages. The organiser reserves the right to make changes to the course. Gathering/start information is listed as 10:00; after finishing, showers and a light meal are available. The number of starting places for Helan and Halvan is limited, to approximately 200 participants. The finish area at Fageråsen includes showers and catering.

name: PRB (Växjö)
description: PRB is a Backyard Ultra event in Växjö, held as a Silver Ticket event in 2026. Participants run a 6,706-metre loop, with a start every hour on the hour. The first start is at 10:00, and the race follows last-person-standing rules based on the general principles of Backyard Ultra. The course is varied and easy to run, combining asphalt and gravel/trails to help runners keep going for as long as possible. The loop turnaround and finish are on the southern shore of Trummen, with services in the turnaround area for runners and their companions.
course_highlights: 6,706-metre loop — 24 loops equal 100 miles (160.93 km)
Approximately 35 metres of elevation gain per loop
Around 3 km of asphalt per loop, with the rest on gravel and trails; the turnaround is on the southern shore of Trummen, close to a playground, skate park and swimming area
additional: The organiser provides an aid table in the turnaround area with sports drink (Umara), water, Coca-Cola, coffee, sweets, crisps and fruit. A cooked meal is served every six hours, with the first serving after four hours. Anyone who completes at least one loop receives a medal from Yoga Wood and a Finisher Beer from Tomorrow Brewing. Participants may set up small tents and chairs in the turnaround area. The nearest bus stop is Trummenvägen (route 3), and the recommended parking is at Ica Kvantum Teleborg (fee: ~10 SEK/day). Participants who choose to withdraw must notify the race management to receive a result. You may not cross the start line and turn back, as the course is one-way, but you may cross the line to change clothes, eat, use the toilet, etc. The race information indicates that public transport and parking are nearby.

name: ÖTILLÖ Gothenburg
description: ÖTILLÖ Swimrun Gothenburg is a well-established swimrun race in the southern Gothenburg archipelago, rooted in a strong local tradition. The event offers three distances—Experience, Sprint and World Series—with varied running and many short open-water swims between granite islands. The start and finish area at Styrsö Bratten is easy to reach by frequent ferry services, and the organiser highlights spectator-friendly views and a summer-friendly race format. The schedule and practical information (ferries, race bib collection and more) are published on the race website ahead of the races.
course_highlights: Frequent transitions between land and water, with many short, intense swim sections (island hopping)
Varied terrain on granite islands: fast trails, rocks and hilly sections
Spectator-friendly and easy to reach, with several daily ferry departures to Styrsö Bratten
additional: Schedule and practical information: race bib collection at the gym at Styrsöskolan (Friday 16:00–17:00 for Experience/Sprint/World Series; Saturday morning according to the timetable); fixed ferry times are recommended (departures from Stenpiren/Saltholmen to Styrsö Bratten). The World Series entry fee includes timing, live tracking if needed, a safety plan with safety boats at swim sections, aid stations along the course, and free post-race food and drink at the finish. Distance-specific details: World Series ~39,200 m (29 running, 28 swimming), Sprint ~22,400 m (18 running, 17 swimming), Experience ~8,800 m (8 running, 7 swimming). Start and finish at Styrsö Brattenbadet; ferry services from Saltholmen or Stenpiren provide access to the race area; limited parking at Saltholmen; use of public transport and the Västtrafik To Go app for ferry tickets and schedules is recommended. Plan your journey in advance and arrive at the start area in good time.

name: TGS - Trail Genom Skåne
description: TGS – Trail Through Skåne is a trail race featuring beautiful trails in Göinge and Hovdala Nature Reserve, starting and finishing at Trädhuset (Hovdala, Hässleholm). The race offers four distances (TGS 60, 35, 25 and 10), with TGS 60 run over two loops (35+25). The new 2026 route is more technical and has a reduced amount of asphalt (under 3 km), bringing runners closer to nature. The race is suitable for runners of different levels who want to enjoy forest terrain and well-marked courses.
course_highlights: Run on beautiful trails in Göinge and Hovdala Nature Reserve
TGS 60 consists of two loops (35+25); the course is more technical, with under 3 km of asphalt
Aid stations at km 13.2 and 24.6; start/finish at Trädhuset (Hovdala)
additional: Start and finish at Trädhuset (Hovdala, Hässleholm). TGS 60: 61.7 km with 1,060 m D+ / D- (maximum time 9h15min, cut-off at the loop point at 13:30). TGS 35: 35.1 km, 600 m+/-, starts at 09:30, finish closes at 17:00. TGS 25: 26.6 km, 460 m+/-, starts at 10:45, finish closes at 17:00. TGS 10: 10.2 km, 200 m+/-, starts at 13:45. Aid stations (VK) offer food, water, cola and sports drink (listed at km 13.2 and 24.6 depending on the distance). Registration is binding after payment; the organizer recommends that runners take out recreational race insurance. Start: The Treehouse/Trädhuset at Hovdala; various distances (50, 25/27, 10 km); restrictions include no trekking poles and carrying a mobile phone, water and energy; maximum times/cut-off times as stated on the website; free parking near the start/finish; aid stations as needed on hot days; results and food after the race.

name: Halland Ultra Beach Trailrun
organizer: Benen på Ryggen Adventures; Svalhögens IF
description: Halland Ultra-Beach (HUB) is a coastal ultrarunning event in the West Coast landscape that celebrates free trail running. The race consists of six stages between Gothenburg and Båstad, offering distances from individual stages (40–72 km) to the full race at 100 km, 100 miles and 200 miles. The routes often follow the shoreline and vary between sand, trails, pastures and more rugged terrain; runners navigate using digital maps/GPX and are largely self-sufficient between checkpoints. The organisers provide stations with warmth, food and energy from Umara, as well as some baggage transport and drop-bag services for the longer distances.
course_highlights: Six stages along the West Coast between Gothenburg and Båstad, mostly close to the shoreline
Varied terrain: beaches, trails, pastures and sections without clear tracks (some water crossings occur)
Largely off-trail and unmarked—navigate using a digital map/GPX (keep the sea on your right)
additional: Early-bird discount applies until 2025-09-30; registration is open until 2026-07-26, with very limited opportunities to register late. Maximum entries: 60 places for 200M and 100M; 30 places per individual stage. For 100k, 100M and 200M, some food and drop-bag service are provided at the end of each stage. The race pack includes a digital map, roadbook and GPX file; baggage transfer to the finish and hot food/drinks at checkpoints and the finish are provided. The race is largely self-sufficient between checkpoints and partly unmarked. Umara energy products are available at the stations; the race pack includes maps, a digital route description and GPX files. Hub Femdagars offers five daily stages (75/64/51/51/87 km), with accommodation options and pacing and guidance services; registration for Femdagars is via Race-ID.

name: Ölands Marathon
description: Öland Marathon is an open marathon starting and finishing in the square in Löttorp. The course is very flat and easy to run, entirely paved, and offers views of Blå Jungfrun. The race consists of an inner loop of 2.1 km and an outer loop of 11.2 km, repeated three times until the distance of 42.195 km is reached. The race is organised by Högby IF and is aimed at recreational runners and masters categories in the stated divisions.
course_highlights: Very flat, easy-to-run marathon course
100% paved, officially measured by federation course measurer Carl‑Gustaf Nilsson
Start and finish in the square in Löttorp; a 2.1 km inner loop plus an 11.2 km outer loop repeated 3 times, with views of Blå Jungfrun
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 12:00. There are three aid stations per lap (approx. 13.3 km), serving sports drink (Umara), Coca-Cola and water; personal energy supplies must be handed in no later than one hour before the start. All finishers receive a medal/fossil made of Öland limestone; ÖM medals go to the top two in each category. The women’s and men’s winners receive dinner for two at Kalk in Löttorp. Accommodation is available in four-bed cabins at Högby IP. Aid stations: three per lap. The course consists of a 2.1 km section in Löttorp followed by an 11.2 km section: Löttorp - Alvedsjö - Kalmarsund - Gudesjö - Löttorp, repeated three times for a total of 42.195 km. Start and finish in the square in Löttorp; accommodation information is available via links on the organiser’s website.

name: Svartåloppet
description: Svartåloppet is a recurring running event held on the second Saturday in August, bringing together runners over several distances. The event offers 14 km and 5.5 km on hilly forest roads and trails, as well as a flat 2.5 km route on roads. The start and finish are at Svartå Folketshus, and timing is provided by Racetimer, delivering modern and reliable results. The event welcomes both recreational and competitive runners and highlights the local landscape and trail network.
course_highlights: 14 km and 5.5 km: hilly forest course on forest roads and trails
2.5 km: flatter route on roads
Start and finish at Svartå Folketshus
additional: Timing for Svartåloppet is provided by Racetimer, and results from previous years are published via Racetimer. The event is held annually on the second Saturday in August. The website contact is listed as Svartå Utvecklingsgrupp, telephone number 076 3073096. Three distances; children's race includes a medal and bag of sweets; on-site registration is available at the stated times (09:00–10:30), according to the event information.

name: Arctic Circle Race
price_range: 2480 SEK inklusive helikoptertransfer; 1490 SEK utan helikoptertransfer
description: Arctic Circle Race is a trail race in the heart of the mountains, where participants are flown by helicopter to the start at Guijaure and run approximately 18 km along the Arctic Circle back to civilisation. The race combines adventure and competition and offers the choice of a helicopter transfer or hiking to the start independently. The course is technical and varied, with narrow trails, rocky slabs and a short but steep climb called “the Wall”. Arctic Circle Race 2026 takes place on Saturday, 8 August, and prices are listed separately for participants with and without a helicopter transfer.
course_highlights: Helicopter drop-off at the start at Guijaure, followed by a run along the Arctic Circle (approx. 18 km).
Varied, rocky and often narrow mountain terrain, with the steep climb known as “the Wall” at ~8 km and the final ~4 km running sharply downhill.
Two water stations (approx. 6 km and 12 km); start at 690 m above sea level, highest point at 805 m above sea level, finish at 480 m above sea level.
additional: Optional helicopter transfer (with or without helicopter). Share a helicopter by registering several participants at the same time — sequential bib numbers and the same start time. Check-in, parking and helicopter pick-up at Camp Polcirkeln, Polcirkeln 3, 93894 Arjeplog. Timing is done using a chip integrated into the bib. First aid and staff are available at the water stations, and a helicopter is on standby for serious incidents. Includes a helicopter to the start and the option of a round trip between Arjeplog and Camp Polcirkeln for 500 SEK, according to the information on the English-language page.

name: Bunketorp Backyard Ultra Trail
description: Bunketorp Backyard Ultra Trail is a “last-man-standing” race in Backyard Ultra format, where participants run a 6,706-metre lap every hour on the hour until only one runner remains. The course in Bunketorp, Lindome (south of Gothenburg), runs entirely through woodland on well-trodden trails, with no asphalt or gravel, and features varied, hilly terrain. The race is organised by IK Uven and has a personal, family-friendly setup with good facilities for both runners and accompanying guests. The 2026 race starts on Saturday, 8 August 2026 at 10:00.
course_highlights: Lap distance: 6,706 metres (Backyard Ultra rules)
Soft forest trails without asphalt or gravel, and no long straight sections
Approximately 140 m of elevation gain per lap, with three distinct major climbs
additional: The organiser provides changing rooms with showers and a sauna, at least seven toilets (including portable toilets), 3–5 participant tents, and space for personal tents. The race office handles bibs, valuables storage and results; a staffed aid station is available throughout the race, and simple refreshments are sold to spectators. First aid supplies and a defibrillator are available at the venue (there is no trained medical staff). There is no age limit; participation is at the participant’s own risk. Race rules: laps are one-way, participants must be in the starting corral at every hourly start and must inform the race office if they withdraw. Prizes are awarded to the top three women, the top three men and the best team (3 runners). Participants start every hour and must complete a lap within the hour; 6,706 m per lap; 120 starting places; Silver Ticket for 2026; results reported to DUV; aid station, drinks, hot food at certain times, changing facilities, toilets, showers and sauna.

name: Nätra Fjällskogslopp
location: Hinnsjöstugan, Nätra fjällskog, Örnsköldsviks kommun, Sweden
description: Nätra Fjällskogslopp is organised by Nätra GIF ungdom and is a scenic trail race held at Hinnsjöstugan in Nätra fjällskog. The first race took place in 2021, and the event offers challenging but enjoyable courses through forests, over boardwalks across wetlands and along winding trails with beautiful views. There are four distances (22 km, 15 km, 9 km and 2 km for children), and the organisers encourage both competitive runners and recreational runners to choose their place in the field according to their ability. The start and finish are at Hinnsjöstugan, with clear markings and services for participants.
course_highlights: Trails, forest roads and boardwalks across wetlands—varied trail running
Views from Västerselsbodarna and Västanåhöjden (with a chance to glimpse Ulvön)
Long downhill stretches towards the finish, with views over Hinnsjön
additional: Organiser: Nätra GIF ungdom. Start location: Startstugan Hinnsjön (address: Hinnsjön 100, Sidensjö). Parking is signposted along the road near Hinnsjöstugan, a short walk from the start. Race bibs must be collected by 09:00 at the latest for the 22 km, 15 km and 9 km races. A bag drop is available at Hinnsjöstugan. Recommended equipment: mobile phone, fluids/energy and a course map. Start times: 22 km 09:30, 15 km 09:45, 9 km 10:00, 2 km 10:10. Course markings use different colours (22/15 km: blue/yellow; 9 km: red/yellow; 2 km: yellow). Participants are asked to stay on the marked trails, use the boardwalks and take their rubbish to the finish. The route passes through two nature reserves (Västanåhöjden and Stakamyras), which have special regulations. Distances are 22 km, 15 km, 9 km and 2 km (children). Start times according to the information: 22 km 9:30, 15 km 9:45, 9 km 10:00, 2 km 10:10. The event runs as a full-day activity from 10:30 to 16:00 and is stated to be fully booked.

name: Ångaloppet Trail
description: Ångaloppet is a welcoming swimrun event at Ånga gård, with the aim of making “swimrun for everyone.” The 2026 races take place on 8 August and include several distances and events for different levels, including 22 km, 11 km, Trail, 5 km and Family. The courses feature varied landscapes with forest trails, gravel roads and hilly, technical terrain; the swimrun races also include several swim sections in both lake and sea. The organisers emphasise a welcoming atmosphere for participants of all ages and experience levels.
course_highlights: Varied forest, trails and gravel roads
Hilly, technical terrain suited to trail running
Located between Lake Ången and the Baltic Sea—combining running and swimming (for the swimrun distances)
additional: In 2026, the event comprises five races on the same day (8 August): 22 km, 11 km, Trail, 5 km and Family. The 22 km race is a loop course (11 km per lap), with approximately 20 swim sections in total (the longest about 190 m and the shortest about 30 m), six aid stations along the course and a cutoff of 2.5 hours at the lap point. Team changes are possible for a fee of 400 SEK—email info@angaloppet.se. The courses are marked, and start group 1 (the earliest start) is listed at 10:00. Ångaloppet Trail is a new distance in the 2026 programme. Team changes are possible for a fee of 400 SEK. More information about equipment, safety, accommodation and parking is available on the event pages.

name: Kräftivalloppet
description: Kräftivalloppet is a running event in Tidaholm that is part of Kraftivalen and takes place near Gamla torget. Registration for the adult race is required via motionsloppet.se, while the children’s and senior races do not require advance registration. Warm-ups before the races are held in collaboration with Hälsocenter, and the event is open to the whole family. The children’s race for ages 7 and up is approximately 600 metres per lap (up to three laps); the rollator and senior races are approximately 600 metres; and the race for children from age 2 is approximately 400 metres.
course_highlights: Part of Kraftivalen in Tidaholm, with the start and event area around Gamla torget
Advance registration via motionsloppet.se is required for the adult race; the children’s and senior races do not require advance registration
Short children’s and senior races, with distances of approximately 400–600 metres per lap
additional: Warm-up before the races with Hälsocenter

name: Istrun - Skaras snabba halvmara
description: Istrun – Skara’s Fast Half Marathon is a half marathon organised by Istrums SK - Friidrott in Skara. The race name highlights that the course is fast and is aimed at runners who want to run a fast half marathon. The race is currently full, but the organiser offers a waiting list for interested runners. For questions or to join the waiting list, runners are asked to email istrun@istrumssk.se.
course_highlights: Half marathon in Skara (promoted as “Skara’s Fast Half Marathon”)
additional: The race is currently full; interested runners can join the waiting list by emailing istrun@istrumssk.se. All information about the race refers to Istrums SK - Friidrott. Entries are handled through RaceID, and runners who are not members of a club are advised to register in M Motion or K Motion, according to the page. PB note: a participant mentions a PB of 1:47.29 in a Facebook post.

name: Häv och Gräv Vikbovändan 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: vuxen 470 kr (fram till den 30/6, sedan kostar loppet 520 kr)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: duoklass: 940 kr per par (fram till den 30/6, sedan kostar duolopp 1040 kr)

description: Häv & Gräv Vikbovändan is a summer event on Vikbolandet in Östergötland where participants can choose to run or cycle. The main course is approximately 45 km long and runs mostly on paved roads and gravel (about 50/50), with several aid stations and samples from local farms along the way. There are categories for runners, cyclists, duos and children, and the event has a clear focus on local producers and an authentic farm setting. Pre-registered participants receive a collapsible cup (folding cup), which they must bring during the event to avoid disposable cups.
course_highlights: Main course approximately 45 km, about 50/50 gravel and asphalt
Aid stations at several local farms, with delicacies and opportunities to visit the farms
Opportunities to meet and sample products at farms with animals (ostriches, alpacas and yaks)
additional: The number of participants in the main event is limited (300). Online registration is open until 4 August; late registration is available from 09:00 in the start area until 30 minutes before each start (if places are available). Pre-registered participants receive a collapsible cup, which must be used during the event. The children's race (approximately 700 m or 1,400 m) requires no advance registration and is free for participants thanks to sponsorship from ICA (children receive a medal and ice cream). Toilets and showers are available at APPTEK's premises (open approximately 09:30–18:30). The running category is timed, with prizes for the top three women and men; the cycling and duo categories have special rules (helmets are compulsory, e-bikes are not allowed, and duo partners may swap as often as they like but must stay within 100 m of each other). There is a group warm-up before the start. Aid stations offer water and sports drinks; pre-registered participants receive a collapsible cup; everyone receives a medal; the event is not sanctioned by the Swedish Athletics Association; helmets are compulsory for cycling; the start and finish are in a floodlit trail setting; medical staff are on site; image rights rules apply. Register at vikbovandan.se/472-2/ or via the registration page on the main website.

name: Kivijärviloppet
description: Kivijärviloppet is a traditional cross-country race organized by Kivijärvi IF since 1970. The event is held in the village of Kivijärvi in the Torne Valley and has grown to more than 200 participants. The main event is the 12 km open class for both women and men, and the race is known for its generous prize table thanks to its sponsors. Many well-known skiers and runners have taken part over the years, giving the race strong local and national standing.
course_highlights: Cross-country race with courses marked in different colors: 0.5 km and 1.5 km (yellow), 5 km (white), 7.5 km (blue), 12 km (red)
The race takes place in the beautiful Torne Valley in eastern Norrbotten
The courses have remained unchanged since the race began in 1970, except during the COVID pandemic
additional: Course routes are marked in different colors for each distance: 0.5 km and 1.5 km (yellow), 5 km (white), 7.5 km (blue), 12 km (red). The event offers a generous prize table for children, adults, and recreational runners, thanks to generous sponsors. The race offers several categories, including a 12 km open class, and is known for its prize money and for bringing together participants of different ability levels. The course runs mainly along natural forest trails.

name: Storå 6 timmars och 3 timmars
location: Guldsmedshyttan, Lindesberg Municipality, Örebro County, Sweden

name: Kullamilen
location: Höganäs friidrottsarena, Höganäs kommun, Skåne län, Sweden
description: KullaMilen is a welcoming running event in Höganäs, with distances for children, recreational runners and veterans. The event offers 2.5 km for children/youth, 5 km for walkers or runners, and 10 km (competitive and recreational classes), starting and finishing at Höganäs athletics arena. The event is organised by Höganäs Friidrott together with local clubs and is part of the Skånska veterancupen for veteran classes choosing to compete. The event emphasises community and the joy of being active, from beginners to experienced runners.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Höganäs athletics arena; a fast course with plenty of running along the Öresund coast
The 10 km course is officially measured and sanctioned by the Skånes Friidrottsförbund; the 5 km shares the 10 km course but turns back earlier
The 2.5 km children’s course runs partly through Lerbergsskogen; asphalt and gravel surfaces, marked by course marshals
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the Race Office at the athletics arena from 09:30 and no later than 30 minutes before each start; race numbers must be worn on the chest. Water stations are located at approximately 3.5 km and 6.5 km, as well as at the finish. All participants receive a medal; prizes are awarded to the best in each class, and there is a prize draw. The prize-giving takes place in the start/finish area. Changing rooms and showers are approximately 75 metres from the finish; light refreshments are sold at the arena. Results are published at www.hoganasfriidrott.se and www.kullamilen.se. Red Cross medical staff will be on site. Part of the Skånska veterancupen; registration is open at a reduced price until 1 April.

name: Blodomloppet (Jönköping)
description: Welcome to Blodomloppet in Jönköping—a recreational event highlighting the need for blood donation, where you can walk, jog or run. In Jönköping, timed 5 km and 10 km races are offered, as well as an untimed 5 km walk. Children can take part in Lilla Blodomloppet (approx. 700 m), which has a mass start and a medal. Participants enter in teams, and the event traditionally ends with a picnic.
course_highlights: Distances: timed 5 km and 10 km races, plus an untimed 5 km walk
Lilla Blodomloppet: approximately 700 m for children up to 12 years old, with a mass start and medal; starts from Knektaparken
Event area at Knektaparken, with a traditional group picnic after the finish
additional: Team entries consist of 3–5 participants; registered blood donors receive a 40 kr discount if they indicate this when registering. Changes (e.g. from 10 km to 5 km) cost 50 kr; show your order ID when collecting your race pack. For registration on race day (11 August), payment is accepted only by Swish or cash. Other payment terms are 30 days, with several payment options (Swish, card via Swedbank Pay, postal giro, invoice). Team and individual entries have different prices; discounts are available for blood donors, and an invoice fee applies. Race numbers can be collected at Hovslätts IK’s clubhouse or at the start. The awards ceremony takes place at 19:30.

name: Vetlanda Citylopp

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Dam-, herr- och motionsklassen (10 km och 5 km) 180 kr

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Kids F8/P8 - F12/P12 (1 km till 1,7 km) 100 kr

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Föreningar (max 15st per anmälan) 900 kr (Föreningar kan anmäla i F/P8-F/P12 samt Junior 5km)

description: Vetlanda Citylopp is an open, spectator-friendly city race taking place on 14 August 2026, with the start and finish on Storgatan in Vetlanda. Runners can choose between 5 km and 10 km on a fast, looped course. There are also several children’s and youth classes, as well as a Funkis class. Bib collection and late registration are available at Stortorget from 12:00 on race day, and the event includes activities and simple food service in the square. Photos and videos will be taken during the race and may be used in future marketing.
course_highlights: Start and finish on Storgatan in central Vetlanda
Fast, spectator-friendly looped course (5 km or 10 km)
Children’s and youth distances from 400 m to 1.7 km, plus Funkis 1 km
additional: Bib collection and late registration are available at Stortorget from 12:00 on race day. Late registration is available until 30 minutes before each start time. Payment on site can be made via Swish (a surcharge applies for late registration). Timing is provided by Racetimer using a chip in the bib, and results are published live on Racetimer’s website and on the OK Njudung website. The event includes activities and simple food service in the square; the organizer will take photos and videos during the race. Participants can walk, jog or run at their own pace. On-site late registration is available for a fee. Photos and videos taken during the race may be used for marketing.

name: Trail- & Ultravasan (Vasaloppet)
description: Vasaloppet organises a summer week of running and mountain biking, including races such as Ultravasan and Trailvasan. The events take place in mid-August and attract tens of thousands of registered participants each year. Registration and practical information are available at vasaloppet.se. The event is organised by Vasaloppet, a non-profit organisation owned by IFK Mora and Sälens IF.
course_highlights: Part of Vasaloppet’s summer week of running and mountain biking
Includes the Ultravasan 90 and Trailvasan (10/30) distances in mid-August
Organised by Vasaloppet (owned by IFK Mora and Sälens IF)
additional: Registration is through Vasaloppet’s registration pages at vasaloppet.se; registering early means a lower price. For company registrations and group bookings, contact foretag@vasaloppet.se. Vasaloppet customer service can be reached by phone at 0250-392 00, and general enquiries at info@vasaloppet.se. Ultravasan 90 is part of Vasaloppstrippeln 90; bib and chip collection is in Mora/Sälen; baggage transport to Mora and Evertsberg; medals and an award ceremony are promised. Trailvasan 10 has a maximum of 1,000 participants, an age limit of 11+, and a start opportunity until 18:15; there are two water/aid stations along the course.

name: BAMM
location: Björkliden, Kiruna Municipality, Norrbotten County, Sweden
description: BAMM (Björkliden Arctic Mountain Marathon) is a mountain orienteering competition in the Björkliden/Riksgränsen area, where participants compete in pairs (men’s, women’s or mixed teams). The competition takes place across large areas of unmarked mountain terrain and is geared towards adventure and orienteering in a mountain environment. The event is presented in collaboration with its main partner, OMM, and the competition website includes practical information about travel, accommodation and the programme. The event is aimed at orienteers seeking a challenging competition experience in an Arctic mountain setting.
course_highlights: Mountain orienteering across large areas of unmarked mountain terrain
Competition format: pairs (men’s, women’s or mixed teams)
Held in the Björkliden/Riksgränsen mountain region near the Norwegian border
additional: Practical travel information is available on the website: transfers can be booked from Kiruna Airport to Hotell Riksgränsen (with connections to SAS/Norwegian flights), as well as return transfers. Travel by train via SJ to Riksgränsen takes approximately 18 hours from Stockholm, and Riksgränsen railway station is about 100 metres from Hotell Riksgränsen. The website also includes the programme and participant list for BAMM 2026, as well as accommodation and Arctic Skibus information. Two-day mountain orienteering in the Björkliden area; mandatory personal and team equipment; approximately 230 starting teams per edition; BAMM 30 includes transport of tent and sleeping-bag equipment to the overnight camp; registration via ReadySetGo.

name: Trail- & Ultravasan
location: Sälen and Mora, Dalarna County, Sweden
description: Ultravasan 90 is a challenging ultramarathon that follows the classic Vasaloppet Trail from Sälen to Mora. The race starts early in the morning in Berga by and offers a scenic, historic running experience through pine forests, winding waterways and summer pasture farms. Participants can enjoy a well-organised race with several aid stations and the option to transport change-of-clothes bags to different checkpoints. Ultravasan 90 is part of Vasaloppstrippeln and attracts runners from around the world who want to test their endurance on a spectacular course.
course_highlights: Start in Berga by, Sälen, with sunrise over the marshes at Smågan
7 official checkpoints with drinks and energy, including Evertsberg, where drop bags can be collected
Scenic pine forests, winding waterways and summer pasture farms along the entire course
additional: Race numbers and timing chips can be collected in Sälen or Mora the day before, or at the start area. The start corrals open at 04:30. Change-of-clothes bags can be dropped off in Sälen for transport to Mora or Evertsberg. Toilets and medical care are available at all checkpoints and in the start and finish areas. Massage is offered in Evertsberg and Hökberg. Official checkpoints with drinks and energy are located at Smågan, Mångsbodarna, Risberg, Evertsberg, Oxberg, Hökberg and Eldris. The event is part of Vasaloppstrippeln. Trail ultramarathon, checkpoints, gear transport, medals, start in Sälen, finish in Mora, Swedish Championship status 2026, maximum 2500 participants

name: Ultravasan
description: Ultravasan 90 is a trail race starting in Berga by, Sälen, offering runners the classic Vasaloppet route through scenic summer landscapes. The race starts at dawn at 05:00 and follows the historic checkpoints to the finish in Mora, with views of pine forests, waterways, trails and traditional mountain farm settings. The race is 92 km long, has Swedish Championship status in 2026 and is part of Vasaloppstrippeln; the maximum number of participants is 2,500, and the minimum age is 17.
course_highlights: Dawn start at 05:00 in Berga by—watch the sun rise over the marshes around Smågan
Seven Vasaloppet checkpoints along the course, with drinks, energy, toilets and medical care
Scenic stretches through open pine forests, winding waterways, well-trodden trails and picturesque traditional mountain farm settings
additional: Race bibs and chips can be collected in Mora or Sälen in the days before the race, or at the start venue. Start pens open at 04:30, and your time starts when you cross the start line. Baggage transport to Mora is available, and you can send a change-of-clothes bag to Evertsberg. There are refreshment stations approximately every five kilometres, as well as toilets and medical care at all checkpoints. Maximum 2,500 participants; training grants of SEK 60,000 are awarded to the winner in each of the women’s and men’s categories. Ultravasan consists of two longer ultramarathon distances: Ultravasan 90 (Sälen–Mora, approximately 92 km) and Ultravasan 45 (Oxberg–Mora, approximately 45 km). Both finish in Mora and are part of Vasaloppet’s Summer Week.

name: Tavelsjö Halvmarathon
description: Tavelsjö Half Marathon takes place on 15 August 2026 and is a pleasant summer event welcoming both runners and families. In addition to the half marathon, there is a timed youth race (2.2 km) and Tavelsjö Mini for children, making the event family-friendly. The start and finish are at Tavelsjö Church, and the organisers encourage early registration.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Tavelsjö Church
The youth race is 2.2 km long and is timed
Family-friendly event with Tavelsjö Mini for children
additional: Registration is open and is listed as closing by 15 August. The youth race is for ages 8–17, starts at 10:00, is timed, and participants receive a medal and something to eat; a prize is also drawn among the participants. Tavelsjö Mini is a popular children’s race, and gift cards are available to buy by logging in (delivery within one week of ordering). Registration opens ahead of the race; gift cards are available; parking is available at Klacken (the clubhouse), between the start and finish; race bibs can be collected during the week before the race or on race day from 09:00 to 10:45.

name: Midnattsloppet Stockholm
description: Midnattsloppet Stockholm is a festive evening race on Södermalm, taking place on 15 August 2026. It offers 21 km, 10 km and 5 km races, as well as several children’s and adaptive races. Late start times, music, spectators and activities along the course create a unique, lively atmosphere. The 21 km race covers two laps of the Midnattsloppet 10 km course, which is described as relatively hilly. The organisers highlight community, the joy of running, and the event’s appeal to both competitive runners and recreational participants.
course_highlights: 21 km = two laps of the Midnattsloppet 10 km course around Södermalm
A relatively hilly course, with climbs and the character of the neighbourhood
Music, samba rhythms and spectators along the course create a festival atmosphere
additional: Start area/warm-up: Ringvägen 26. Finish: Hornsgatan 57. The entry fee includes, among other things, a Björn Borg T-shirt (this year’s colour/design), chip timing, sports drink and water along the course, and a cold Vitamin Well, fruit and an energy bar at the finish. A medal can be purchased when registering, and a digital certificate is available. The organisers accept wellness benefits from Benifex, Epassi and Benefits, and provide instructions for using a voucher code; team registration gives a discount of SEK 50 per person. Information about start groups, T-shirts and race packs, as well as dedicated pages for companies, is available on the organisers’ website. The digital Midnattsloppet takes place from 12/9 to 20/9.

name: Vasastafetten
description: Vasastafetten is a festive mass-participation relay race along the classic route from Sälen to Mora. Up to ten runners share a total distance of approximately 92 km, with legs ranging from 4.5 to 15 km. The race welcomes elite runners and recreational participants, as well as teams from clubs, companies and groups of friends. The start is in Berga by in Sälen, and the event is one of the oldest competitions of the summer week. The 2026 start time is 08:00 on August 15.
course_highlights: Trail race along the classic Sälen–Mora route
Ten legs of approximately 4.5–15 km (approximately 92 km in total)
Starts in Berga (Sälen) and finishes in Mora
